To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

selected reaction monitoring mass spectrometry (SRM) can quantitatively determine proteins by specific targeting and allows the determination and measurement of multiple proteins in a single analysis.

we developed a novel method to measure multiple mitochondrial proteins in a single sample and we used it to show that patients carrying mutations in the BCKDHA and BCKDHB genes have reduced levels of E1α, E1β, E2 and E3 proteins in mitochondria.
SRM is a valuable tool to quantify proteins in mitochondria-enriched samples from patients with maple syrup urine disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins in the mitochondria of healthy individuals and patients suffering from MSUD.
the development of new analytical tools for protein analysis in the field of inherited disorders.
the development of a method that allows the quantification of multiple proteins in the mitochondria‐enveloped cells of patients with MSUD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRM is a powerful method for the quantification of proteins and can be used to elucidate disease mechanisms.
SRM is a very useful and reliable tool to quantify disease‐associated proteins.
SRM is an excellent tool to measure the levels of proteins and to study the effects of mutations and pharmacological interventions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SRM is a very useful method to quantitatively measure disease-associated proteins in cultured cells and to elucidate the effect of mutations on the protein levels.
SRM is a powerful and reliable tool to quantify disease‐associated proteins.
SRM is a valuable tool to investigate protein effects of mutations, which cannot be assessed by RNA analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SRM is a powerful tool to study the protein effects of disease‐associated mutations and to quantify multiple proteins in one sample.
SRM is a valuable method for the analysis of disease-associated proteins, especially when the disease is caused by multiple proteins, as in MSUD.
SRM can be used for reliable and accurate quantification of proteins in cultured cells and tissues.
